title: Add read-only expected-version fences to atomic store decisions
description: Foundational prerequisite for atomic graph.request_expansion persistence. Extend SqliteEventStore.commitExpectedVersionDecisionLegs so the primary leg remains an append and a later leg with an empty events array is an audited read-only expected-version fence checked under the same BEGIN IMMEDIATE transaction before any append. The fence must move no aggregate version and write no event/receipt, while accepted and rejected decision evidence remains strict and replayable. Generic commit and an empty primary leg remain invalid.
definitionOfDone: Re-measure the public multi-leg contracts, validation order, request digest, receipt namespace, transaction, decision roster persistence/read decoder, and SQLite schema before editing; if a mixed append/fence decision cannot be represented and strictly reread without an unsafe migration or authority weakening, report blocked rather than inventing a parallel store path.

TDD pins the public semantics: leg 0 requires at least one event; each later leg is either a normal append or, only when events is exactly empty, a read-only expected-version fence. Generic commitExpectedVersionDecision and commit continue refusing empty events with STORE_INPUT_INVALID, duplicate aggregate IDs and MAX_DECISION_LEGS still count every append/fence leg, and hostile/mutable input is snapshotted once in the existing validation precedence.

An accepted append-plus-fence decision checks every aggregate version inside the same BEGIN IMMEDIATE transaction before the first write, appends only event-bearing legs, leaves the fenced aggregate version/events unchanged, persists an auditable roster entry with no receipt for the fence, and the strict decision reader plus close/reopen replay accepts exactly that mixed roster.

A stale or racing fence rejects the whole decision with the store's exact EXPECTED_VERSION_CONFLICT reason/disposition targeting the fenced aggregate and performs zero event writes on every append leg; concurrent/interleaving SQLite tests prove goal/graph movement cannot slip between fence validation and append.

Idempotent replay returns byte-identical durable evidence with no extra writes; reusing the same decision key with a different fence aggregate/version conflicts; receipt identifiers are reserved only for append legs and accepted mixed rosters cannot mask a missing primary receipt or forged secondary receipt.

Publish the behavior through the existing @moe/store root without adding a second authority API, keep production files focused at the repository size targets, and pass fresh foreground pnpm --filter @moe/store typecheck, pnpm --filter @moe/store test, pnpm verify:store, pnpm typecheck, and pnpm test gates with explicit exit codes.
taskRails: Store foundation only: do not edit daemon expansion code in this leaf.
A fence is observation, not an event: it must create no aggregate row, version increment, event row, or receipt; its durable audit is the decision request/roster.
All append and fence expected versions are checked under one SQLite write lock before any event append. No preflight-then-commit split and no caller-side emulation.

Preserve the existing public input shape, fail-closed validation precedence, immutable snapshots, request-digest/idempotency binding, duplicate-aggregate rule, and MAX_DECISION_LEGS cap unless current-byte exploration proves a type-safe additive contract is necessary.

Do not weaken strict decision evidence: accepted decisions still require a real primary append receipt; null receipts are permitted only for verified read-only fence legs, while non-null receipts remain fully cross-checked.
No schema migration unless current schema is proven incapable; if migration is required, stop and report the measured scope before widening this leaf.
